Problem name: 10k-C100

Problem family: online_bin_packing

In an online one-dimensional bin packing problem, 10000 items arrive one at a time in the order listed in the items table. Each item has an integer size and must be irrevocably assigned to one currently open bin or to a new bin when it arrives. Every bin has capacity 100, and the sum of item sizes assigned to any bin cannot exceed this capacity. The objective is to minimize the total number of bins used after all items have been packed.

Instance parameters:
{
  "capacity": 100,
  "n": 10000
}

Data files are provided under this instance directory. Your code will be executed from the instance directory, so read the relative paths below directly.
Load the required CSV tables at runtime from the exact relative paths below; do not hardcode CSV rows or table values in the code.
- items (./data/items.csv)
  Exact CSV columns: ["item_id", "size"]
  Data rows (excluding header): 10000
  Description: A table with columns `item_id` and `size`. Rows are sorted by online arrival order; `size` is the integer size of the item. There are no missing values.

Determine the optimal objective value for this instance.

Problem name: bier127

Problem family: traveling_salesman_problem

In a symmetric Euclidean traveling salesman problem, a salesperson must visit each of 127 cities exactly once and return to the starting city. The travel cost between each pair of cities is given in the distance matrix derived using the TSPLIB EUC_2D rounding rule. The objective is to find a Hamiltonian cycle with minimum total travel distance.

Instance parameters:
{
  "n": 127
}

Data files are provided under this instance directory. Your code will be executed from the instance directory, so read the relative paths below directly.
Load the required CSV tables at runtime from the exact relative paths below; do not hardcode CSV rows or table values in the code.

  Exact CSV columns: ["city_id", "x", "y"]
  Data rows (excluding header): 127
  Description: A table with columns `city_id`, `x`, and `y`. It gives the Euclidean coordinates of each city from the TSPLIB instance. There are no missing values.
- distance_matrix (./data/distance_matrix.csv)
  Exact CSV columns: ["from_city_id", "to_city_id", "distance"]
  Data rows (excluding header): 16129
  Description: A complete directed representation of the symmetric distance matrix with columns `from_city_id`, `to_city_id`, and `distance`. Diagonal rows have distance 0; off-diagonal distances are symmetric. Distances are computed with the TSPLIB EUC_2D rounding rule. There are no missing values.

Determine the optimal objective value for this instance.

Problem name: n100m10

Problem family: flow_shop_scheduling

In a permutation flow shop scheduling problem, 100 jobs must be processed on 10 machines in the same machine order from machine 1 through machine 10. Each job has a specified processing time on each machine. A machine can process at most one job at a time, and a job can be processed on at most one machine at a time. The decision is a single job permutation used on every machine. The objective is to minimize the makespan, defined as the completion time of the last job on the last machine.

Instance parameters:
{
  "m": 10,
  "n": 100
}

Data files are provided under this instance directory. Your code will be executed from the instance directory, so read the relative paths below directly.
Load the required CSV tables at runtime from the exact relative paths below; do not hardcode CSV rows or table values in the code.
- processing_times (./data/processing_times.csv)
  Exact CSV columns: ["job_id", "machine_1", "machine_2", "machine_3", "machine_4", "machine_5", "machine_6", "machine_7", "machine_8", "machine_9", "machine_10"]
  Data rows (excluding header): 100
  Description: A wide table with one row per job. Columns are `job_id` followed by `machine_1`, `machine_2`, etc.; each machine column gives the processing time of that job on that machine. There are no missing values.
- operations (./data/operations.csv)
  Exact CSV columns: ["job_id", "machine_id", "processing_time"]
  Data rows (excluding header): 1000
  Description: A long table with columns `job_id`, `machine_id`, and `processing_time`. Each row gives the processing time for one job-machine operation. There are no missing values.

Determine the optimal objective value for this instance.
